A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Max-Former/Max-ResNet research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–F and checklists support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments, architectural ablations, and training/inference resource measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and adds ANN-counterpart results and further CIFAR-100 ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed architectures, LIF neurons, pooling/DWC/SSA components, membrane shortcuts and input processing remain unchanged in Section 3, Table 1 and Appendix A.3. New Table 7 configurations are experimental variants, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, CIFAR10-DVS and DVS128 Gesture under the same classification tasks and input conditions. Added model variants use existing CIFAR coverage; the new discussion of non-hierarchical transformers does not introduce a new test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces Transformer (ANN) with Max-Former (ANN), retaining ResNet-19 and the existing SNN comparators. Table 7 also adds SDSA-based comparisons. Meta-Spikformer remains an evaluated baseline despite its corrected citation.

E3.justification: Table 7 adds controlled configurations varying first-stage pooling, Embed-1Max placement and SSA/SDSA token mixing. These extend the experimental design under the retained Table 6 settings; existing splits, training budgets, resolutions and metrics are not revised.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Table 7 groups (6)–(8), examining additional pooling placements and embedding variants under SSA and SDSA. This extends existing architectural ablations. The resource analysis, shortcut analysis and GradCAM examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and retain checklist item 7's explanation that error bars were omitted because of computational expense. No seed counts, repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the Transformer ANN's CIFAR-10/100 results of 96.73%/81.02% with 96.82%/82.41% for a different Max-Former ANN model. Table 7 adds results including 79.98% and 78.78% for first-stage pooling variants and 81.77%/81.52% for SDSA. Existing headline and resource-measurement results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The neuron equations, low-pass transfer-function derivations, linearization assumptions and energy formulas are retained. The added appendix interpretations introduce no new mathematical definition, proof or formal correction.

C1.justification: The frequency-bias explanation, claimed network-level low-pass proof, architectural contributions and headline performance claims are retained. Although the conclusion changes 'Spiking Transformers' to 'SNNs,' v3's abstract and introduction already make the broader SNN claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly argues that patch-embedding enhancement has limited persistence in non-hierarchical transformers and suggests optimizing token mixing instead. Appendix F interprets earlier pooling/convolution choices through frequency bias. Existing manual-balancing and hardware-deployment limitations remain.

D1.justification: The SpikingJelly implementation, Table 6 hyperparameters, A30/H20 hardware disclosures, timing setup and code-access statements are retained. New experimental variant names are not accompanied by substantive implementation definitions or additional reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: Appendix F adds discussion of Spike-Driven Transformer and newly cited Spikformer v2, positioning the frequency analysis as an explanation of their architectural choices. Table 3 also corrects Meta-Spikformer's source to Spike-Driven Transformer v2; the broader related-work narrative is unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to conclusion terminology, acknowledgements and expanded appendix discussion. Appendix F becomes 'Impact and Limitation.' The introduction, method narrative and overall section structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: Table 7 expands from five to eight groups, with local formatting and emphasis changes. Appendix material reflows, and the unchanged GradCAM Figure 8 moves from PDF page 19 to page 20. Existing architecture diagrams and spectral figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 7's additional first-stage pooling controls better support selective pooling placement, while Table 2 supplies an ANN counterpart and Appendix A.2 clarifies an applicability boundary. These are limited gains: the central theory and results remain unchanged, new variants lack full implementation definitions, and uncertainty reporting is still absent.
